description: closePgPool sets _pool = null and then awaits p.end(); a concurrent getPgDb() during that in-flight await sees _pool === null and creates a fresh Pool, so the just-created pool is never drained and the connections from the closing pool may leak.
reason: Mechanism is real — closePgPool nulls _db (145) and _pool (148) synchronously before `await p.end()` (149), so a getPgDb() racing during the await would build a new pool/_db; but the only production callers (scripts/firestore-export-to-pg.ts:1501, scripts/reconcile-migration.ts:701) invoke it in CLI shutdown finally blocks where no concurrent getPgDb() is expected, so impact is negligible.

description: readNumber is called for DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS and DB_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS without allowZero, so setting either to 0 (pg's documented value to disable the timeout) throws 'Invalid ...' instead of disabling it.
reason: Lines 82-83 call readNumber without the third allowZero arg (unlike DB_POOL_MIN on line 80 which passes true), so the `n === 0 && !allowZero` guard at line 59 throws `Invalid DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS: 0`, making pg's documented 0-disables-timeout value unreachable via env var.
